variants.name: Structured Task cancellation
variants.implementation_notes: Swift builds cancellation into its concurrency model: Task.cancel() sets a Boolean cancellation state on the task (no reason, no forced kill), Task.isCancelled/Task.checkCancellation() observe it, throwing suspend points such as Task.sleep surface CancellationError, and withTaskCancellationHandler runs an onCancel closure immediately - including when the task was already cancelled before the handler was installed. Structured children (task groups, async let) are cancelled with their parent, while unstructured and detached tasks must be cancelled explicitly. For resources that are not async-aware, withTaskCancellationHandler plus an interruptible underlying operation is the bridge.
pitfalls: Task.cancel() only sets a flag: a loop that never checks isCancelled and never awaits a cancellable operation runs to completion, and dropping the task reference removes the only handle to cancel it.
onCancel runs concurrently and immediately, possibly before the handler body starts, so it must be thread-safe, idempotent, and must not touch task-local state or assume the operation has begun.
Cancellation does not propagate to unstructured Task {} children or detached tasks - only structured children follow their parent, and every detached task needs its own cancel call.
Swallowing CancellationError (returning normally instead of rethrowing) makes a cancelled task look successful; treat it as control flow and rethrow or return an explicit cancelled result.

variants.name: Combine AnyCancellable subscriptions
variants.idiom_name: AnyCancellable / Cancellable.cancel() as the cancellation token
variants.implementation_notes: Before Swift concurrency, Combine already provided a token-shaped abstraction: AnyCancellable is documented as a type-erased cancellation token for a subscription, cancel() tears the subscription down (and the upstream stops producing), and the instance cancels automatically on deinit - which makes subscription lifetime ownership the cancellation mechanism. This fits reactive pipelines and callback code, and it composes badly with async/await work that does not run inside the pipeline; for new asynchronous code prefer Task cancellation and use Combine only at the reactive boundary.
variants.code_sketch:
var cancellables = Set<AnyCancellable>()

publisher
    .sink { value in handle(value) }        // subscription starts
    .store(in: &cancellables)               // token owned by the storage

cancellables.removeAll()                    // cancel: deinit/subscription teardown
pitfalls: An AnyCancellable that is never stored is deallocated immediately and cancels the subscription at once - a classic silent no-op where nothing is delivered.
Deinit-driven cancellation makes the lifetime implicit: moving a cancellable between scopes (or into a collection that outlives the view) silently changes when the pipeline stops.
Combining cancellables does not propagate task cancellation: a cancelled Task does not tear down Combine subscriptions unless the code bridges explicitly, and vice versa.
